title: Friendship theorem (Erdős–Rényi–Sós windmill) — formalize-only
why_not_classical: Erdős–Rényi–Sós 1966 friendship theorem is completely settled for FINITE graphs: if every two distinct vertices have exactly one common neighbour, then some vertex is adjacent to all others (and the graph is a Dutch windmill of triangles). Infinite counterexamples exist and are OUT OF SCOPE. This is not an open problem. Value is a Mathlib/SimpleGraph contribution. Do NOT re-fund as novel. A 2025 arXiv rewrite via Lovász ϑ is irrelevant — we want the classical finite theorem, not a new proof paper.
recommendation: Shortlist #2 — genuinely NEW proof layer over closed Ramsey/clique work. Hypothesis is a common-neighbour condition (card = 1 for EVERY pair, adjacent or not), not a clique-Ramsey statement. Mathlib v4.10.0 already has SimpleGraph.commonNeighbors, card_commonNeighbors, IsSRGWith, and AdjMatrix — none of those files prove the friendship theorem (zero 'friendship'/'windmill' hits). Partial ladder: (A) windmill graphs satisfy the hypothesis; (B) a universal vertex of degree n-1 forces the windmill-of-triangles shape; (C) no-universal-friend ⇒ regular ⇒ SRG with λ=μ=1 ⇒ contradiction. Prefer Huneke-style combinatorial counting; AdjMatrix/SRG path allowed because IsSRGWith.matrix_eq already exists. Cap: do not require a general theory of strongly regular graphs beyond λ=μ=1.

statement_pin_required.convention: G : SimpleGraph V with V finite nonempty. Hypothesis: ∀ {v w : V}, v ≠ w → Fintype.card (G.commonNeighbors v w) = 1. Conclusion (v1): ∃ u, G.degree u = Fintype.card V - 1. Optional v1-b: G is a windmill of triangles (every block a 3-cycle through u, edge-disjoint).
landmines: FINITE is load-bearing — the statement is false for some infinite graphs. Pin Fintype V.
The condition applies to adjacent AND non-adjacent pairs. Restricting to non-edges is a different theorem.
Simple graphs only (no loops, no multis). Isolated-vertex / |V|≤2 edge cases must not sneak into the main lemma.
Do not conflate with Ramsey R(3,3) (cliques under 2-colourings) or with IsSRGWith in general; friendship is the special case λ=μ=1 plus the pre-regularity argument.
Linear-algebra/eigenvalue proofs are optional; prefer combinatorial Huneke/Mertzios if budget is tight.
statement_pin_required.canonical_source: P. Erdős, A. Rényi, V. T. Sós, On a problem of graph theory, Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. 1 (1966) 215–235 (Theorem 6). Combinatorial expositions: C. Huneke, The friendship theorem, Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 192–194.

feasibility_shape: Level A: definitions + windmill construction satisfies the hypothesis + small F_n native_decide sanity (optional). Level B: universal-friend ⇒ windmill-of-triangles. Level C: no universal friend ⇒ regular of degree k ⇒ IsSRGWith n k 1 1 ⇒ n = k*k - k + 1 ⇒ contradiction (counting or AdjMatrix). Two-heartbeat cap; stop after universal-friend if Level C overruns.
